turns.content: A star has a measured parallax of 2 milliarcseconds and will be compared with the same star placed at 20 pc. Convert the parallax to arcseconds. No measurement uncertainty is supplied.
Use the distance relation appropriate to the stated observation to find the star's original distance in parsecs.
State how the received photon flux scales with distance when the star's intrinsic luminosity is unchanged.
Use the original and new distances to calculate the factor by which the observed flux changes.
State the best-supported brightness factor, retaining uncertainty from the unreported measurement error and rounding.
Check the factor by converting the distance ratio to a magnitude difference and back to a flux ratio.
Report the brightness-change factor and briefly identify the relation used in the calculation.
